interpretation: Two real raw-file drainers used no live decoder pipe. One ended naturally after 18.84 seconds and 109 complete frames with clean offline decode; the other remained for 60 seconds until the host bound, with 703 complete frames and a host-cut terminal tail. All 109 overlapping complete frames were identical; verified complete prefixes decode cleanly. UART observed generation overrun for remote port 59282 after 18.8 seconds, while remote port 59283 ran 60.1 seconds until host close. No sampled zero send window: minimum 65535. Port 59282 lastack stayed 3807210838 at 26521, 27701 and 28901 ms; nrtx was 1 and cwnd 1440 at 28901 ms, with 31680 unsent and 1440 unacked bytes. ACKs later advanced slowly and generation overrun disconnected. This identifies open-window ACK/retransmission congestion in sampled TCP state, not where packets or ACKs were delayed or lost. The board sees the subnet-router peer; local socket mapping to translated ports was not recorded. Flat capture counters and a short successful peer duration do not establish requested endurance or worst-case input. Shazam stayed off and source was quiet.
